subject: Trial sprint plan & data access checklist — SummitWare
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Amir Patel <amir.patel@summitware.com>, Caroline Moss <caroline.moss@summitware.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Trial sprint plan & data access checklist — SummitWare

Hi Amir & Caroline,

Thanks again for the call earlier — helpful to walk through the integration surface and your immediate priorities. Below is a concise recap, proposed three-week "trial sprint" scope, success metrics, owners, and the access steps we need to start. Please confirm any corrections and whether the proposed kickoff week (Nov 16) works for you.

Key pain points (as discussed)
- Customer support agents are spending ~6–8 minutes per ticket on manual triage; need reliable intent classification + suggested responses.
- Latency variability from current vendor is causing timeouts in the UI (spikes during peak hours).
- Hard to evaluate answer quality across your internal KB and compliance constraints (PII removal).

Trial sprint goals (3 weeks)
- Integrate a Redwood-hosted inference endpoint with your ticketing export (subset).
- Measure latency (p95) and closed-loop utility (agent accept rate of suggestions).
- Produce a small prompt/eval suite (100 sample tickets) and run automatic quality checks.

Success metrics (pass/fail thresholds)
- Latency: p95 <= 350 ms for 1-token warm path (target); aim to be under 300 ms for final acceptance.
- Agent acceptance: >= 40% suggestion acceptance on pilot samples.
- Safety/PII: no raw customer PII persisted in logs; redaction pipeline validated on sample set.

Scope & owners
- Redwood: integration support (Ben) + CS onboarding (Grace) + solution design (Karthik).
- SummitWare: data export owner (Amir) + security contact (Caroline) + legal for contracts.

High-level timeline (proposed)
- Week 0 (Nov 16): access & environment setup — S3 bucket link, allowlist, service account.
- Week 1 (Nov 23): integration + initial model runs on subset.
- Week 2 (Nov 30): prompt tuning, run evals, handoff results & next steps.

Immediate access/setup checklist (what we need from SummitWare)
1) S3 export with 2,000 anonymized tickets (or dataset export to secure Sharepoint) — deliver link to redwood-trial@summitware.com.
2) IP allowlist and one service account with minimal permissions (details in attachment).
3) Confirmation of retention/logging policy preference (default: 30 days masked logs).
4) SOC2 questionnaire / security contact for quick review.

Attachments: trial-scope.xlsx (detailed task list), mutual-action-plan.docx (M.A.P.).

Next steps
- If you confirm the access items and Nov 16 kickoff, we’ll schedule the 60-min tech kickoff and share a weekly check-in cadence (Tuesdays).
- Grace will lead onboarding once access is provided; Karthik will run model/config tuning.

If anything above is off, please flag edits inline.

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192

From: Caroline Moss <caroline.moss@summitware.com>

Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Trial sprint plan & data access checklist — SummitWare

Thanks Ben — great summary. A few items to clarify from our side before we lock the Nov 16 start: 

1) Data sensitivity & retention: the sample export will include customer-reported PII fields that Legal requires redaction for. Can you confirm Redwood's default retention window and whether logs include any raw payloads? We prefer masked logs and an option to have logs disabled for the pilot.

2) SOC2 evidence: we need a copy of your latest SOC 2 report or an equivalent attestation to share with our security team. Can you attach?

3) Contract & MSA: Legal will want to see your standard MSA and data processing addendum. Please send to legal@summitware.com and CC me.

4) Timeline: we have an internal change freeze on Nov 12–15. Can we plan to begin Nov 16 as you proposed (fine), but push the kickoff meeting to Nov 17 to give Legal a day to confirm?

5) Cost estimate: can you provide an approximate TCO for the 3-week sprint (hosted) so we can include it in our budget note?

If you can answer 1–3 and share the docs, I’ll route to Legal and Security. Otherwise looks good.

Best,
Caroline
Director, Security & Compliance
Caroline.Moss@summitware.com

Caroline — thanks for the quick review. Short answers below and next steps at the end.

1) Retention & logs: Default pilot policy is 30 days masked logs; we can disable logging entirely for the pilot or arrange customer-managed KMS for any artifacts. No raw payloads are persisted outside encrypted storage. I’m attaching a short SOC2 summary and the redacted logging options.

2) SOC2: attaching redwood-soc2-report.pdf (summary) and I’ll ask our security lead to provide the formal report under NDA if Legal requires it.

3) MSA/DPA: I’ve asked our contracts team to send the standard MSA to legal@summitware.com and CC you; expect that by end of day.

4) Timeline: Nov 17 for the kickoff meeting works fine — I’ll update the internal calendar.

5) Cost: ballpark for the hosted 3-week sprint (pilot infra + support) is $12–18k depending on throughput and dataset size. We’ll provide a more precise estimate once we see sample volume.

Attachments: redwood-soc2-report.pdf (summary), trial-scope.xlsx (updated).

Action items
- Ben: share SOC2 summary + confirm MSA dispatch (in flight).
- Amir: provide sample export or a test subset link by Nov 12.
- Caroline: copy legal@summitware.com on any incoming contract e-mails.
- Grace: stand by to schedule onboarding when access is provided.

Thanks — I’ll wait for Amir’s sample link and will confirm the Nov 17 kickoff invite.

Ben Carter
